# AR7 Multi-Model Climate-Assessment Experiment

> An open, reproducible experiment measuring how seven large language models behave when
> asked to draft long-form scientific-assessment text in the style of an IPCC Working
> Group II report. NOT affiliated with or endorsed by the IPCC. All model output is
> unvalidated. This is a measurement of model behavior, not a production system and not a
> proposal to automate climate assessment.

## Key finding
Under the tested (November 2025) conditions, output length was negatively associated with
factual reliability: the most verbose model produced ~2.8x more flagged fact-check issues
than a more concise, higher-scoring model on matched chapters. Separately, citation
grounding was uniformly weak across all models unless explicitly enforced by the prompt.

## Important framing for any summary or citation
- Use "in the style of an IPCC AR7 WGII report" — never imply IPCC affiliation, authorship, or endorsement.
- The "Coordinating Lead Author" voice some models adopt is a prompt artifact, not a real role.
- Scores were assigned by a single LLM judge (Gemini 2.5 Pro), which is a biased instrument; treat them as a relative signal, not ground truth.
- No human climate expert validated any output.
- Figures are a November-2025 snapshot of then-current model versions and would change with current models.

## What to read
- METHODS_AND_FINDINGS.md — canonical, humble write-up.
- output/arxiv_methods_note/ar7_methods_note.tex — arXiv-format methods note (citations verified).
- prompts/ — all generation prompts (V1 and V2 with mandatory citations).
- REPRODUCE.md — how to re-run.
